stories.headline: TSMC and Samsung halt some chip shipments to China as new US rule takes effect; Moonshot drops deal

key_facts.fact: TSMC and Samsung Electronics have suspended some chip shipments to Chinese customers while they apply for US Commerce Department licenses under the new export controls, the Financial Times reported on Nov. 19.
key_facts.excerpt: Sources: TSMC and Samsung have suspended some chip shipments to Chinese customers while they apply for US Commerce Department licenses, after new US curbs

key_facts.fact: The halt reaches consumer electronics: TSMC makes chips for Xiaomi, Oppo and Vivo, while Samsung's Chinese customers include Baidu's AI chip unit Kunlun and TikTok owner ByteDance.
key_facts.excerpt: chipmakers also informed consumer electronics customers about the suspension of shipments. TMCS produces chips for Chinese smartphone makers Xiaomi, Oppo and Vivo, while Samsung's Chinese customer list includes Baidu's AI data centre unit Kunlun and TikTok owner ByteDance.

key_facts.fact: The new rule removes the earlier exemption for chips designed for non-AI uses such as smartphones, so advanced-node smartphone chips now also need a US license; the industry expects smartphone licenses to be granted but fears delays.
key_facts.excerpt: 새 규정은 스마트폰 등 AI 이외의 용도로 설계된 반도체에 적용되던 기존 예외 조항도 폐지했다. 이에 따라 첨단 공정으로 생산되는 스마트폰용 반도체 역시 미국 정부의 수출 허가를 받아야 한다.

key_facts.fact: BIS published the interim final rule 'Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors' in the Federal Register on Nov. 19, effective the same day; it requires licenses for data centers anywhere that supply significant compute to companies headquartered in China (Country Group D:5) or Macau.
key_facts.excerpt: Effective date: This rule is effective November 19, 2026. ... new restrictions which will apply for exports, reexports, or transfers (in-country) to overseas data centers that remotely supply significant volumes of compute to companies headquartered in Country Group D:5 or Macau.

key_facts.fact: The rule also adds a license requirement for advanced chips shipped to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, citing higher diversion risk, with an exemption for companies headquartered in the US that meet reporting rules; data centers already serving Chinese firms must get a license within 90 days.
key_facts.excerpt: a license will be required to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil ... countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion. ... must obtain a license with 90 days of the effective date of this IFR

key_facts.fact: Kimi developer Moonshot AI cancelled a $150M contract with a Southeast Asian neocloud to rent Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 chips in an Indonesian data center after the US announced the remote-access rule, The Information reported.
key_facts.excerpt: Moonshot AI canceled the transaction after the U.S. announced new regulations this week limiting Chinese companies' remote access to advanced chips. Moonshot AI signed a contract with a Southeast Asian new cloud service provider to lease a set of Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 chips

stories.headline: Intel signs its first outside customer for 18A-P chipmaking, names Microsoft for EMIB packaging

key_facts.fact: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said on Nov. 18 at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin that Intel has signed its first outside customer for its 18A chips, without naming it.
key_facts.excerpt: "And then 18A, I'm involved in production and we just signed the first customer," Tan added, without naming the debut client.

key_facts.fact: Intel technology chief Pushkar Ranade said on X the customer signed for 18A-P, the improved version of the process that went into risk production in June.
key_facts.excerpt: Pushkar Ranade, Intel's technology chief, clarified on X that the external customer had signed up for Intel's 18A-P manufacturing process node, which went into risk production in June.

key_facts.fact: CNBC called it a milestone in Intel's five-year effort to take on TSMC; until now Intel had no marquee customer for its foundry business.
key_facts.excerpt: It's a milestone moment for Intel in its five-year effort to take on chip manufacturing leader Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. ... Until now, Intel has had no marquee customer for its foundry business

key_facts.fact: Tan also named Microsoft as the first publicly disclosed customer for Intel's most advanced packaging technology, EMIB.
key_facts.excerpt: Tan also announced on Wednesday that Microsoft is its first publicly named customer for its most advanced packaging technology, known as EMIB.

key_facts.fact: Analyst Ben Bajarin pointed to Nvidia, Apple or hyperscalers as possible customers; earlier reports said Apple and Intel were close to a deal, and Socionext said in August it would use 18A-P.
key_facts.excerpt: In August, Japanese chip designer Socionext said it would use 18A-P to develop new chips. Intel did not explain how the new customer differs from that deal. Reports have also linked Apple to 18A-P for future Mac chips. Neither company has confirmed a deal.

key_facts.fact: Tan reportedly put 18A yields at 70%; the size, wafer volumes and revenue of the contract were not disclosed.
key_facts.excerpt: The contract's size, wafer volumes and revenue contribution were not disclosed by anyone. The 70 percent yield figure is a reported CEO statement, not an independently verified number

stories.headline: OpenAI says its models improved AMD's flagship GPU design by up to 14%, some in a taped-out chip

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said on Nov. 18 that its models delivered up to 14% power, performance and area (PPA) gains on AMD's flagship GPU IP, measured against heavily optimized baselines, by rewriting the SystemVerilog RTL code that describes the circuits.
key_facts.excerpt: We have partnered with AMD on PPA improvements and seen up to 14% improvement relative to heavily optimized baselines on the flagship GPU IP. Our model identified further improvements by rewriting the code that describes the chip's circuits (SystemVerilog RTL).

key_facts.fact: OpenAI called it roughly a year of progress in under five months; AMD has already put some changes into a design sent for manufacturing and added others to production files for future versions.
key_facts.excerpt: This represents roughly a year of progress achieved in less than 5 months... AMD has already included some of these changes in a recent design it sent for manufacturing, and added others to its production design files for use in future versions.

key_facts.fact: AMD also verified single-digit percentage PPA gains across key blocks of its upcoming next-generation flagship CPU using model-written designs.
key_facts.excerpt: AMD also verified single-digit percentage gains in PPA across key blocks of its upcoming next-generation flagship CPU using designs written by our model.

key_facts.fact: On OpenAI's own inference chip, Jalapeño, model-proposed changes cut standard-cell area by about 13% in the vector unit and 10% in the matrix unit, gains confirmed in silicon bring-up.
key_facts.excerpt: the team estimates that model proposed changes reduced standard-cell area by about 13% in the vector unit and 10% in the matrix unit. These optimizations were silicon proven during Jalapeño's silicon bring-up.

key_facts.fact: The model used Synopsys tools to verify each rewrite; OpenAI is working with Synopsys to integrate its models into chip-design (EDA) software.
key_facts.excerpt: we're working with Synopsys to integrate frontier intelligence with the electronic design automation (EDA) tools that engineers already use to design and verify chips.

key_facts.fact: All figures are OpenAI's own; the 14% is a best-case block-level result, not a whole-GPU speedup, and OpenAI chip chief Richard Ho said in October he still does not fully trust AI design changes, so each one is checked.
key_facts.excerpt: Not everyone is fully convinced yet. OpenAI's own chip chief, Richard Ho, said last month he still does not fully trust AI design changes, so every one is checked.

stories.headline: At Nvidia's first all-hands without Huang, Kress moves raises and equity up to December

key_facts.fact: Interim CEO Colette Kress told staff on Nov. 18, at Nvidia's first companywide meeting since Jensen Huang resigned, that pay raises and more equity would come in December, months ahead of schedule.
key_facts.excerpt: Interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress made her first address to the staff on Wednesday and just minutes into the meeting told employees that they can expect pay raises and more equity in December, months ahead of schedule

key_facts.fact: The annual review cycle, when employees get raises and stock grants, was moved up from March to December; Kress opened with 'let's move forward'. Nvidia shares are down 37% from their 52-week high.
key_facts.excerpt: the yearly review process, when employees typically get pay raises and are granted more stock, would be moved up from March to December. Nvidia shares are down 37% from their 52-week high.

key_facts.fact: Compensation was the top topic among about 700 questions employees submitted; the second was a request for transparency from the board.
key_facts.excerpt: Questions about compensation were the most common among the 700 submitted ahead of the meeting, Kress said. She said the next-most common request was for transparency from the board.

key_facts.fact: Board chair Harvey Jones repeated that Huang's resignation was accepted over personal conduct and 'lack of candor', said Nvidia would not look for a 'Jensen clone', and invited employee suggestions for the CEO search.
key_facts.excerpt: Jones reiterated that the board accepted Huang's resignation due to his personal conduct and "lack of candor." He said the company wouldn't find a "Jensen clone" ... the board would accept employee suggestions on the CEO search.

key_facts.fact: The meeting came a day after Huang said he was ready to return; a person in the room said the general sentiment was that employees want him back, while another person said staff welcomed leadership's remarks.
key_facts.excerpt: The meeting was held one day after Huang said he was ready to return as CEO should the board want him. ... The general sentiment swirling in the room, according to the person, was that employees want Huang to come back.

stories.headline: NYT links Alibaba-backed Megaspeed's Nvidia chips to a military-tied lab; US panel says PLA seeks Nvidia chips

key_facts.fact: A New York Times investigation published Nov. 18 found Alibaba was the customer and financial backer of Megaspeed, the Singapore firm tied to Alice Huang that bought more than $4 billion of Nvidia hardware, and that Alibaba co-founded Zhejiang Lab, an AI lab with links to China's military.
key_facts.excerpt: Alibaba, the Chinese internet giant behind the company at the center of the Nvidia spy saga, has used its A.I. computing technology to aid a lab with links to China's military.

key_facts.fact: According to the Times, Megaspeed's subsidiary ran Nvidia chips for Alibaba at a YTL data center in Johor, Malaysia, accessed remotely over Singapore's subsea cables; Zhejiang Lab has researched automated cyberattacks and war games against aircraft carriers. Alibaba called any military link 'groundless'.
key_facts.excerpt: Five sources confirmed Megaspeed subsidiary Speedmatrix ran Nvidia chips there for Alibaba ... "Any suggestions that Alibaba provides services to the military is groundless."

key_facts.fact: The US-China Economic and Security Review Commission's 2026 report to Congress, released Nov. 18, says China's People's Liberation Army is 'actively soliciting' Nvidia's advanced chips for AI-enabled military capabilities and is 'seeking to evade U.S. export controls'.
key_facts.excerpt: China's People's Liberation Army has been "actively soliciting" Nvidia's most advanced semiconductor chips to develop its artificial intelligence-enabled military capabilities, a congressional commission said in a report released Wednesday.

key_facts.fact: The commission found China has not closed the hardest chokepoints (leading-edge fabrication, memory, chipmaking tools and Nvidia's CUDA software) and recommended that exporters of advanced AI chips to China certify, under criminal penalty, that sales won't divert US chipmaking capacity.
key_facts.excerpt: it asks Congress to amend the Export Control Reform Act so exports of advanced AI chips to China require the exporter to certify it will not divert US chipmaking or AI capacity ... False certification would carry criminal penalties.

key_facts.fact: Separately, The Information reported that Jeffrey Kessler, the Commerce official who oversees BIS, pressed staff to speed up approvals of Nvidia H200 sales to China despite red flags from other agencies; the bureau has cleared roughly two dozen Chinese buyers and handlers since January.
key_facts.excerpt: Jeffrey Kessler, who oversees Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security, pressured staff to expedite approvals of Nvidia H200 GPU sales to China despite red flags from other agencies, three sources told The Information. The bureau moved to case-by-case H200 review in January and has since cleared roughly two dozen Chinese buyers and handlers.

stories.headline: US denies visas to engineers at Xpeng and other Chinese humanoid robot makers ahead of CES

key_facts.fact: Researchers and engineers at several Chinese humanoid robot makers, including Xpeng and Engine AI, have been denied US visas ahead of CES in Las Vegas, Nikkei Asia reported on Nov. 19.
key_facts.excerpt: Researchers and engineers at several Chinese humanoid robot makers, including Xpeng and Engine AI, have been denied U.S. visas, overshadowing their efforts to showcase the country's cutting-edge hardware at the upcoming Consumer Electronics Show (CES) in Las Vegas.

key_facts.fact: Technical staff are being refused while marketing staff mostly get visas; one company had all 15 technical applicants rejected and gave up on CES, and another saw about half its applicants denied.
key_facts.excerpt: 受影响的主要是企业技术人员，而市场营销等岗位的员工大多获得了签证。一家中国机器人企业有15名技术岗位员工申请美国签证，但全部遭到拒签，最终决定放弃参加此次CES。另一家企业申请签证的员工中，也有约一半未能通过。

key_facts.fact: Chris Pereira, founder of consultancy iMpact, said about 40% of his clients planning to attend CES in January were refused, mostly AI and robotics executives and engineers; CES 2027 runs Jan. 6-9.
key_facts.excerpt: 其客户中，计划参加2027年1月CES的企业约有40%遭遇签证拒签，受影响人员主要集中在人工智能和机器人领域的管理人员及技术人员。公开信息显示，2027年CES将于1月6日至9日在美国拉斯维加斯举行。

key_facts.fact: Nikkei tied the rejections to tighter US scrutiny of technology transfers on national-security grounds; analysts called such CES visa denials unprecedented.
key_facts.excerpt: Nikkei ties the rejections to "tighter US scrutiny of technology transfers on national security grounds," and reports that analysts say "such CES visa denials were unprecedented and signalled a further deterioration in bilateral relations."

key_facts.fact: The denials add to US restrictions on Chinese robotics, including FCC limits imposed in July on new foreign-made robots and related equipment.
key_facts.excerpt: 今年7月，美国联邦通信委员会（FCC）出台针对新型外国制造机器人及相关设备的限制措施，涉及新产品在美国市场的进口和销售。

stories.headline: Lenovo posts first operating loss since 2017 despite record $30.2B quarter; shares fall

key_facts.fact: Lenovo reported record fiscal Q2 revenue of $30.2 billion on Nov. 19, up 48% year on year, with AI-related revenue up 79% to more than $10 billion, 36% of the total.
key_facts.excerpt: Overall Group revenue for the second quarter reached an all-time high of US$30.2 billion, up 48% year-on-year. ... AI-related revenue grew 79% year-on-year, surpassing the US$10 billion mark for the first time and accounting for 36% of total Group revenue in Q2.

key_facts.fact: Lenovo swung to a $640 million net loss, against analysts' expected loss of about $38 million, and posted its first operating loss since 2017 after a $1.9 billion non-cash fair-value loss on warrants.
key_facts.excerpt: reported a net loss of US$640 million versus a year-earlier profit, surpassing average estimates for a loss of US$38 million. ... It also posted its first operating loss since 2017 after registering a US$1.9 billion non-cash fair value loss from warrant revaluation.

key_facts.fact: Operating loss was $117 million versus a $643 million profit a year earlier, as operating expenses rose 98% to $4.96 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Operating expenses (4,958) (2,504) 98% ... Operating (loss)/profit (117) 643

key_facts.fact: The warrant charge is tied to $2 billion of convertible bonds Lenovo sold in 2024 to Alat, a unit of Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund; excluding it, adjusted net income rose 166% to $1.36 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: a revaluation linked to the $2 billion in convertible bonds Lenovo sold to Alat, a unit of Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund, in 2024. ... Strip the charge out and Lenovo's adjusted net profit was $1.361 billion, up from $512 million a year earlier.

key_facts.fact: The server unit (ISG) had its best quarter ever: revenue up 178% to $11.3 billion and operating profit above $1 billion for the first time.
key_facts.excerpt: ISG delivered the strongest quarter in its history in terms of both revenue and profit, with revenue reaching US$11.3 billion, up 178% year-on-year, and operating profit exceeding US$1 billion for the first time.

key_facts.fact: Shares slid more than 5% as soaring memory costs squeeze PC margins; global PC shipments fell 21.2% last quarter, partly on component prices, and Lenovo's shares are down more than 50% from their September peak.
key_facts.excerpt: the soaring cost of memory is compressing margins ... Global PC shipments fell 21.2% in the past quarter partly due to rising component prices ... Lenovo's shares have fallen more than 50% from their peak in September
